raw.music: Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)

plan.rationale: Sierra Reads EP. 1 — 'The Inventory.' Sierra performs being someone who claims she's decentered him while every line of denial reveals she has, in fact, been doing exactly the thing she's denying. The 'sixteen times this morning' is the giveaway. 'I am thriving' is the dry button on someone who is clearly not. This is character-comedy not joke-comedy: the audience laughs because they ARE her, not because they got a punchline. Catherine Cohen / Esther Povitsky lane. P37 chin-in-hand deadpan is the perfect contradicting visual — she LOOKS composed while her words betray her.

script_chunks.text: I HAVE NOT DRIVEN BY HIS APARTMENT.
I HAVE NOT VIEWED HIS INSTAGRAM STORY

plan.voiceover_text: Yes. I have decentered him. Here is the inventory. I have not texted him. I have not driven by his apartment. I have not viewed his Instagram story sixteen times this morning. I am thriving.
plan.caption: Yes I have decentered him. Here is the inventory: I have not texted him. I have not driven by his apartment. I have not viewed his Instagram story sixteen times this morning. I am thriving.
comedic_devices_used: character-driven denial — every line is a lie that reveals the truth
specific number reveal ('16 times this morning') — the receipt
the 'I am thriving' dry button on a person who clearly is not
audience identification — they ARE her, that's the laugh
plan.v0_failed: Earlier draft ('Cool. I've been single 18 months. He's decentered. Now what.') — generic deadpan-shrug, no character. Lazy.
plan.v1_failed: Sponsor-read parody ('use code his loss for 15% off Decentered.™') — clever structure, but still concept-comedy not character-comedy. No truth in it. AI-feeling.
plan.v2_thesis: Stop writing jokes. Write a character. The bit is Sierra in denial. Every denial confirms what she denies. The inventory IS the bit. Catherine Cohen-coded.
